statement: Given that $\\sin\\theta+\\sin\\phi=a$ and $\\cos\\theta+\\cos\\phi=b$, show that $\\cos(\\theta-\\phi)=\\dfrac{a^{2}+b^{2}-2}{2}$. Hence find the maximum possible value of $a^{2}+b^{2}$.
solution: Squaring and adding the two given equations: $a^{2}+b^{2}=(\\sin\\theta+\\sin\\phi)^{2}+(\\cos\\theta+\\cos\\phi)^{2}=2+2(\\sin\\theta\\sin\\phi+\\cos\\theta\\cos\\phi)=2+2\\cos(\\theta-\\phi)$. Therefore $\\cos(\\theta-\\phi)=\\frac{a^{2}+b^{2}-2}{2}$. Since $\\cos(\\theta-\\phi)\\le1$, we get $a^{2}+b^{2}\\le4$, with equality when $\\theta=\\phi$. So the maximum possible value of $a^{2}+b^{2}$ is $4$.
hints: Square both equations and add them.
Use sin sin + cos cos = cos(theta-phi).
